haiku-low.q1: They see the generic reply: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent: no link and no email.
haiku-low.q2: They get the same generic reply. No link and no email are created or sent, because the account is over the limit of 3 links per hour.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes and only once. It ends sooner if it is used, or if a newer link is issued for the account.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays live and unused until it expires after 30 minutes, so the user can try again with a valid password.
haiku-low.q5: None. All the account's sessions, including the resetting device, are deleted. The user is redirected to login and must log in manually.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated and put into the email link when the email is queued. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the token and looks up the row by hash. The link is good if it is under 30 minutes old, unused, and not replaced.
haiku-low.q9: It is not a separate counter. It is the count of reset_tokens rows issued for that account in the last hour; the document does not say how old rows are removed.
haiku-low.q10: Earlier live links are marked dead when the new link is issued, in step 1, before the new token row is stored and the email queued.
haiku-low.q11: The password hash is saved, the link is burned, and sessions are deleted; then the "password changed" email is queued. Whether these run as one atomic unit is NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic reply: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent (no link, no email).
sonnet.q2: The limit is 3 links issued in the last rolling hour, so the API does nothing more: no link, no email. The user still gets the same generic reply.
sonnet.q3: A link works for 30 minutes and only once. It ends sooner if it is used, or if a newer link is issued for the account (which kills earlier live links).
sonnet.q4: Still live. The form shows an error and the link stays live until it expires, so the user can try again.
sonnet.q5: None. All of the account's sessions are deleted, including the device that did the reset. The user is redirected to the login page and logs in again with the new password (no automatic login).
sonnet.q6: The email worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told. They get no link and no message, and can only request again. The document lists whether this is acceptable as an open question.
sonnet.q7: The API generates the token (32 random bytes), stores only its hash, and queues the email with the raw token in the link.
sonnet.q8: The API hashes the token and looks for a live row in reset_tokens. A live row is under 30 minutes old, unused, and not replaced. If one is found, the form is shown. Otherwise the "link expired" page is shown. Nothing is changed.
sonnet.q9: In reset_tokens. The count is the number of rows issued for that account in the last hour. Old requests drop out as their issue time falls outside the rolling hour window.
sonnet.q10: Any earlier live link is marked dead (replaced). This happens before the new token row is created and the email is queued, and only after the user lookup and rate-limit checks pass.
sonnet.q11: The new password hash is saved in users, the link is burned in reset_tokens, and all of the account's sessions are deleted. The "password changed" email is queued after those, followed by the redirect to login. Whether they happen in a single transaction is NOT STATED.
